question: What share of SCALE-SHARE's sampled starts of 5 to 20 knots lies in the proved class, what growth classes does the theorem predict there, and do they match SCALE-SHARE's refereed shares and real growth?

public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch job.py; python3 -B merge.py <out dir> <results.json>
public_inputs.reused: SCALE-SHARE scale.py (samples, weights, cluster rule) and runs/scale-share (recorded classes); DOUBLE-IDENT machine_check.py and dims.py (class, theorem rule, model)

forbidden_inputs: Changing a prediction, the class or the rule after reading the frozen run
cheapest_meaningful_control: the cluster rule's classes on the same samples (P1, P2)

predictions.P1: regenerated cluster-rule classes equal SCALE-SHARE's recorded ones
predictions.P2: theorem's class = cluster rule's in the class
predictions.P3: in-class share of non-stalling in [0.55, 0.90] at every size
predictions.P4: in-class dimension 2 >= 75% of growers at every size and higher at 20 than at 5
predictions.P5: dimension >= 3 at most 1% of in-class growers
predictions.P6: 60 regrown in-class samples per size agree round by round to round 6
predictions.P7: in-class dimension-2 share of growers within 5 points of SCALE-SHARE's all-grower share at every size

stop_rule: One run; stop at the table, or the first size where P6 fails.
disclosed_exploration: pilot on seed 99 (200-400 samples at five sizes) and the integrity check on chain 0 at n = 5
